newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Adcock, Prempharm merger signed.
newsitem.headline: Adcock, Prempharm merger signed.

text.p: Adcock Ingram said on Thursday it had purchased 100 percent of the Premier Pharmaceutical Company Ltd with effect from May 1, 1996 -- thereby merging the two companies.
Based on current market capitalisations, the enlarged Adcock will have a market capitalisation of some 5.3 billion rand, Adcock said in a statement.
In order to implement the terms of the offer, Adcock will restructure its share capital by consolidating its ordinary shares on a 1-for-10 basis.
The company will then undertake a capitalisation issue on a 9-for-1 basis with shareholders receiving nine "N" shares for each new ordinary share held, Adcock said.
This will result in each Adcock shareholder holding one new ordinary share and nine "N" shares for every 10 ordinary shares currently held.

In terms of the merger, Adcock will buy all of the Prempharm ordinary shares in issue. It will issue 13.5 new Adcock ordinary shares, 121.5 new Adcock "N" shares and make a cash payment of 41 rand for every 100 Prempharm shares held.
Following the merger Tiger Oats Ltd, the listed subsidiary of C.G. Smith Ltd -- Adcock's controlling shareholder -- will be the largest shareholder in Adcock with a 35.3 percent stake.
Prempharm's controlling shareholder, the Premier Group Ltd, will have an approximate 29.7 percent stake.
Williams, who will remain as chairman of the new company, was upbeat about the future of the merged operation.
"Our strength lies in our depth of management and broad product portfolio. Benefits of critical mass allied to a strong cash base, will ensure quality earnings growth in the years ahead," he said.
